ssr: Math.random() in render (decoherence circles) causes hydration mismatches. Nested components (WaveVisualization/PhaseIndicator) are defined inside render and remount every tick.
fake_complexity: The 'real-time coherence' is Math.random noise plus exponential decay. It does not measure anything.
target: Move to @aura-glass/labs (or remove); use GlassGauge/GlassProgress for real metrics
justification: This is a themed random-number widget with no product use case in a premium design system. It has invalid CSS color math, a style object passed as a className, render-time randomness, a non-reactive main prop, and no meter semantics. Eighteen stories inflate coverage for a novelty.

name: GlassProbabilityCloud
material_impl: OptimizedGlass frosted shell. Canvas colors are hard-coded rgba purple/blue. createGlassStyle({variant}) returns an object that is interpolated into a className template string ('[object Object]'). Fixed 600x400 canvas with no responsive scaling.
motion: A setInterval at 16ms updates React state unconditionally (even when realTimeMode=false and under reduced motion), re-rendering the whole component at about 60fps. The measurement ping honors reduced motion.
a11y: Canvas has no accessible name or text alternative. Emoji-only button labels (👁️ Observe). Interaction is click/hover on canvas only, so it is keyboard-inaccessible.
api: forwardRef, className string concatenation. No displayName.
ssr: 'use client'; canvas in effects; SSR-safe output, but it is CPU-heavy.
fake_complexity: Pseudo-physics on random noise. Default probabilityPoints=[] is a new array each render, so the init effect re-randomizes all particles on every 16ms render. The realTimeMode interval (50ms) depends on quantumTime, so it is torn down every 16ms before it fires and real-time mode never runs. A full-canvas createImageData is allocated each frame.
justification: It is broken by construction: a 60fps React re-render loop re-randomizes particles every tick, the advertised realTimeMode can never fire, it is not responsive, and it is inaccessible. It has no place in a production design system.

name: GlassQuantumField
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell plus bespoke glass-backdrop-blur-md/border-border/20. The canvas has class bg-black but is painted rgba(255,255,255,.18), which is contradictory. Inline style width/height fixed (default 800x600) with no responsive scaling.
motion: A rAF loop does 3-4 setState calls per frame. Because 'render' depends on particles, the effect re-subscribes every frame. Field update is O(nodes x particles) per frame (about 1200x50 at defaults). Reduced motion stops the loop (good). The measurement plays a sound via useGlassSound.
a11y: The control panel is fake: select, ranges and checkboxes all have onChange={() => {}}, so they render as controlled inputs that ignore user input. The canvas has no text alternative. Static ids (quantum-type-select etc.) collide.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. Particle uncertainty is mutated in place inside setState. Many physics props.
fake_complexity: The 'Schrödinger approximation'/'Heisenberg' labels decorate random motion. The controls are visually present but non-functional. The single story hides them (showControls:false, timeEvolution:false, 280x210) so the certification screenshot looks static and tidy.
justification: Its controls ignore input, its render loop costs O(n*m) per frame and re-subscribes every frame, and it is a fixed-size canvas with no semantics. The story is tuned to hide all of this. Remove it from the core package.

name: GlassQuantumTunnel
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell, but every inner surface uses a bespoke neutralGlassStyle object with hard-coded rgba gradients and backdropFilter blur(24px) saturate(1.5): a duplicated material with no tokens. Injects a <style> block with a media query per instance. Uses glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-90/60 classes, which are undefined in src/styles.
motion: setInterval-driven state updates, framer overlays; reduced motion is partially honored. The canvas is 800x300 scaled via CSS (good responsive fallback with a mobile state rail).
a11y: role=region with label. Desktop state overlays are clickable motion.divs (not keyboard reachable). The mobile rail uses real buttons (better). Canvas has no text alternative.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. Default quantumStates=[] is a new array each render, and the init effect calls setQuantumParticles([]) with a new array each time, so rendering without quantumStates loops forever (code-read, not executed).
fake_complexity: Random 'tunneling events'. 'Wave Coherence' is just cos(time).
justification: This is a decorative pseudo-physics demo with a bespoke duplicated material, undefined utility classes, per-instance style injection, and a likely infinite render loop at default props. It has no product role.
evidence: Pixel stats desktop.png: max chroma 21 -> grey-on-white

name: GlassSuperpositionalMenu
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell overridden by an inline backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,.3). Every card and button uses the bespoke menuGlassStyle object (same blur(24px) saturate(1.5) rgba recipe as the Tunnel, copy-pasted).
motion: A 16ms setInterval updates quantumTime forever (even under reduced motion). The QuantumState/WaveFunction/QuantumNoise/EntanglementLines components are defined inside render, so every 16ms tick unmounts and remounts every menu item, destroying framer state, hover, and focus.
a11y: role=menu, but items are non-focusable motion.divs with onClick (no menuitem role, no tabIndex, no keyboard). Action buttons have a nonsensical aria-expanded='true'. Emoji labels (🔬, ⚛, 🔄).
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes. The 'Entangle' button calls currentStates.sort(), mutating state in place. menuStates is copied to state once and never resynced.
fake_complexity: A menu whose items randomly change probability and must be 'measured' to select: an anti-usability gimmick.
justification: It is an inaccessible menu that remounts its items 60 times per second and whose selection model is deliberately random. It contradicts what a design system menu is for.

name: GlassWaveFunction
material_impl: OptimizedGlass frosted shell. createGlassStyle(...).background is passed into className (a garbage class). Canvas strokeStyle is assigned CSS variables ('var(--glass-bg-default)', 'var(--glass-white)'), which canvas cannot resolve, so the assignments are ignored and the grid and interference lines draw in whatever color was set last. A Tailwind arbitrary class is built from a template string (glass-duration-[150ms]), which cannot be compiled. Fixed 800x400 canvas.
motion: A rAF loop gated on realTimeMode && shouldAnimate (the best-behaved in the folder). Wave rows use framer whileHover/whileTap without reduced-motion gating.
a11y: Wave rows are clickable motion.divs with no keyboard or role. Canvas has no text alternative. Amplitude labels are positioned with magic margins.
api: forwardRef, className. No displayName. Props do not extend HTMLAttributes, though ...props is spread.
fake_complexity: Low: it plots real sine and gaussian functions from the given equations. The 'phase space' and 'spectrum' are crude approximations.
target: Move to labs; a real need is covered by the chart family
justification: This is the least broken quantum component (honest plotting, motion-aware rAF), but it is still a fixed-size canvas demo with CSS variables that canvas ignores, and it does not belong in core. Deprecate it into a labs/demo package.

name: QuantumEntanglementVisualizer
material_impl: OptimizedGlass, with raw Tailwind bg-gradient-to-br from-white/10 via-purple-500/15 and per-state emerald/amber/rose Tailwind classes plus backdrop-blur on inner cards. These raw Tailwind classes are not in shipped src/styles. Uses undefined glass-text-primary-opacity-70 classes. glass-gradient-primary is repeated three times in one className.
motion: None (a hover border transition only).
a11y: role=table on a card grid with no rows or cells, which is wrong. The progress bar has no meter semantics. A dl/dt/dd structure is used for metrics (good).
api: Plain function, no forwardRef, no style/props passthrough. Uses '@/lib/utils' cn while every sibling uses lib/utilsComprehensive. Falls back to hard-coded DEFAULT_PAIRS demo data when pairs is empty.
fake_complexity: The name says 'Visualizer', but it is a static card list of demo data. There is no visualization of entanglement.
justification: A static demo-data card with the wrong table role, unshipped Tailwind color classes, an inconsistent API, and no tests. A generic stat/metric card already covers any real need.

name: GlassRating
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (elevation level1) wrapper, optional via glass=false. Star colors are raw Tailwind text-blue-500/purple/green/yellow/red-500 classes, none of which are defined in shipped src/styles, so stars fall back to inherited text color (the screenshot is achromatic, max chroma 28). Sizes w-4..w-10 are Tailwind.
motion: CSS hover:scale-110/active:scale-95, correctly disabled under useReducedMotion.
a11y: radiogroup/radio with roving tabIndex, aria-label per star, arrow keys, Enter/Space, glass-focus and glass-touch-target. Bugs: aria-checked is true for every star <= value (a radio group must have exactly one checked); arrow keys change value but do not move DOM focus; arrow keys step whole stars even with allowHalf; aria-required defaults to true for any non-readOnly rating.
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes, className/style passthrough, unique gradient ids via useId (good). Controlled-only: no defaultValue or internal state, so clicking does nothing without onChange. The custom icon only applies to filled stars and is ignored for half state.
fake_complexity: None.
duplicates: none found in src/components (no other Rating/StarRating)
justification: This is a solid, honest control with the best accessibility scaffolding in the shard, but it is an orphan: it is not exported from src/index.ts or any subpath, so consumers cannot import it. Before export it needs: token-based star colors (the Tailwind color classes do not ship, so stars render grey), single aria-checked, focus that follows arrow keys, half-step keyboard support, and uncontrolled defaultValue support.
evidence: src/index.ts (no GlassRating export; rg finds no reference outside src/components/rating)
src/components/rating/GlassRating.tsx:219-246 (keys change value without moving focus; whole steps)
Pixel stats desktop.png: max chroma 28 -> stars not colored

name: GlassIntelligentSearch
material_impl: Uses the Glass primitive as a wrapper, then overrides it with a 230-line inline <style> block (lines 779-1011) that hard-codes rgba(255,255,255,.2-.35) fills, rgba(255,255,255,.18) borders, a literal blur(24px) saturate(1.5) chain and !important on almost every rule. The slider thumb is hard-coded #94a3b8 and the checkbox uses a hand-drawn SVG data URI. No intent, elevation or tier tokens are used, so the primitive does nothing here.
motion: CSS spin and pulse classes are gated by useReducedMotion (lines 1040, 1061). There is no enter/exit motion for the dropdown or results.
a11y: The suggestion dropdown has role=listbox/option but the input is not a combobox: there is no aria-controls, no aria-activedescendant and no arrow-key navigation, so suggestionRefs is collected but never used (line 489). The 'Search input' aria-label overrides the placeholder. The voice button is labelled only by an emoji plus title. The results count is a polite live region. Inputs are 44px. Emoji icons are used throughout (lines 756-765, 1046, 1067, 1395).
api: Plain React.FC with no forwardRef, no style passthrough and no ...rest. Uncontrolled only: there is no value/onQueryChange, and filters cannot be controlled. maxResults, showFilters and showSuggestions are fine. The prop interface is called IntelligentSearchProps instead of GlassIntelligentSearchProps.
ssr: Has 'use client'. window.webkitSpeechRecognition is only touched in a click handler. No heavy imports.
fake_complexity: The 'NLP' is a substring keyword match for intent ('find', 'vs', 'best'), a stop-word list and a positive/negative word list for 'sentiment' (lines 116-259). Calling this 'natural language' search is overclaiming. It also shows debug-style 'Intent / Entities / Keywords' chips and a raw 'Score: 3.5' to end users (line 1385).
target: Single GlassSearch / GlassCombobox family (with a separate faceted-results recipe)
justification: This is a 1.4k-line monolith that mixes a toy keyword 'NLP' engine, filters, voice and result rendering into one uncontrolled FC, with no ref, no controlled query and an inline stylesheet full of hard-coded white rgba plus !important that bypasses the material system it wraps. The suggestion list has no real combobox keyboard model. The filter and highlight logic is worth keeping as a headless hook. The visual layer should become a recipe on a proper GlassCombobox shared with the five other search components.
screenshot_review: Image rendering through the Read tool returned empty in this session, so the review used grayscale pixel statistics. Desktop luminance mean is 245 with std 19; mobile mean is 247 with std 21 (0-255). A std under about 20 on a mean around 245 means a near-white glass surface on a near-white canvas with very little tonal separation. That is the washed-out white-on-white look, not a premium layered material. The visual score is capped accordingly.

name: GlassSpotlightSearch
material_impl: OptimizedGlass with elevation, but the style prop is overwritten by createGlassStyle({intent:'neutral', elevation:'level2'}) (line 307), so the elevation prop is effectively ignored for fill. Row selection is hard-coded inline rgba(255,255,255,.62/.22) plus a blue rgba(37,99,235,.34) border (lines 404-414).
motion: Uses Tailwind 'transform transition-all scale-100 opacity-100' classes (line 303-304). These are not glass- prefixed and are only present via the storybook shim, and since the component returns null when closed the scale transition never plays. scrollIntoView uses behavior:'smooth' with no reduced-motion check.
a11y: Has role=dialog aria-modal but no focus trap and no focus restore. There is no listbox/option or aria-activedescendant, so screen readers get no announcement of the selected row. Focus is set with a 100ms setTimeout. The keydown handler's effect deps omit filteredActions/handleActionSelect (line 166), so Enter can run a stale result list after typing when selectedIndex stays 0.
api: forwardRef with HTML attribute passthrough. Controlled open/onClose. maxResults, fuzzySearch and groupByCategory are reasonable. localStorage key 'spotlight-recent' is a hard-coded global, which makes instances collide.
ssr: Has 'use client'. createPortal(document.body) runs in render when open, so it would crash if open=true during SSR. localStorage is read in an effect.
fake_complexity: None. The 'fuzzy' match is a subsequence match, which is honest.
target: interactive/GlassCommandPalette (single command-palette primitive)
justification: This is a second command palette that is not exported from root, alongside the exported GlassCommandPalette and GlassSpotlight. It has a real stale-closure bug in its keyboard handler, no focus trap, no ARIA listbox semantics, Tailwind classes that do not ship, and an elevation prop that gets clobbered. Merge its recent-actions and grouping features into the canonical command palette and delete this file.
screenshot_review: Image rendering through the Read tool returned empty in this session, so the review used grayscale pixel statistics. Desktop luminance mean is 244 with std 22; mobile mean is 239 with std 31 (0-255). A std under about 20 on a mean around 245 means a near-white glass surface on a near-white canvas with very little tonal separation. That is the washed-out white-on-white look, not a premium layered material. The visual score is capped accordingly.

name: LiquidGlassSearchField
material_impl: Uses the shared LiquidGlassMaterial primitive, but disables every distinctive feature (refraction, reflection, microInteractions, adaptToMotion, sheen=0) and then overrides its blur with a hard-coded 'blur(16px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.08) contrast(1.04) !important' in an inline <style> (lines 52-53, 70-71). Options use tokenised rgba(var(--glass-color-white)/var(--glass-opacity-10)), which is better.
motion: No motion apart from a transition-property override. There is nothing that needs reduced-motion handling.
a11y: The input has role=combobox and aria-expanded but no aria-controls, aria-activedescendant or arrow-key support, and no Escape handling. A label wraps both the sr-only text and, when minimized, a button, which is an invalid label association. Suggestion buttons have no role=option and sit inside the listbox. 44px min-height is good. There is no visible focus style on the input (outline:none, line 40) beyond the option focus-visible.
api: forwardRef with div passthrough. Semi-controlled value/onValueChange, although internal state still updates when controlled. The placement prop only sets a data attribute (line 133) and has no behaviour. minimized/onMinimizedChange only expands and never collapses. There is no inputRef or input props passthrough.
fake_complexity: placement ('top-trailing', 'center', 'auto') is advertised but not implemented.
target: Become the canonical GlassSearchField/Combobox on LiquidGlassMaterial
justification: This is the right foundation, a small forwardRef on the shared LiquidGlassMaterial, which makes it the best candidate to become the single search field of the 5.0 Liquid Glass line. Today it is incomplete. It has a non-functional placement prop, no keyboard combobox model, label/button nesting, and an !important blur override that fights its own material. It also has only one story, one smoke test and no certification screenshot. Redesign it into a full ARIA combobox (with a headless filter hook shared with GlassIntelligentSearch) and absorb the duplicates.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this target. It is uncertified visually.

name: LiquidGlassSearchTab
material_impl: Pure pass-through to LiquidGlassSearchField with placement='bottom', which has no effect.
motion: None.
a11y: Inherits the field's issues. There is no tabpanel/tab relationship despite the name.
api: forwardRef. 'active' returns null. tabId only becomes a data attribute.
fake_complexity: The name implies tab-bar integration (an iOS 26-style search tab), but the wrapper adds no behaviour.
target: LiquidGlassSearchField (or a LiquidGlassTabBar 'search' slot)
justification: Twenty-five lines that rename props on LiquidGlassSearchField and add only a null-render flag. It inflates the component count without adding capability. If search-in-tab-bar is a real pattern, implement it as a slot on LiquidGlassTabBar.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this target. It is uncertified visually.

name: LiquidGlassShowcase
material_impl: Composes LiquidGlass* components, then globally overrides '.liquid-glass-material' background, border and box-shadow with !important (lines 45-56) and the badge cluster's backdrop-filter. The showcase therefore does not show the real material, it shows a CSS patch. It hard-codes #0f172a/#475569/#737373, a gray gradient background, and inline rgba styles on its own 'Open' button and cards.
motion: Delegated to the children. None of its own.
a11y: A fake listbox of <span role=option> with no keyboard support (lines 340-359). The 'Open' button is about 30px tall. It uses the main landmark, which is wrong for an exported component.
api: No props, no ref, no className. Fixed demo content ('Liquid Study', 'Aura System').
ssr: Has 'use client'. Heavy: it imports eight components into whatever bundle includes it.
fake_complexity: The tagline says 'Production app chrome' and 'Surface intelligence', but it is a static demo page.
target: Move to Storybook/docs-only example (not a package export)
justification: A propless demo page should not ship in the public API, and this one undermines the system by !important-overriding the Liquid Glass material it is meant to show off. That means the showcase misrepresents what consumers get. Keep it as a docs/story composition after the underlying components look right without overrides.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this target. It is uncertified visually.

name: GlassCollaborativeCursor (social)
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell. Labels use createGlassStyle({opacity:0.8}), which sets CSS opacity on the whole label and text and drops text contrast (line 282). There is a hard-coded 15-color neon cursor palette (#FF6B6B etc).
motion: framer-motion. The reduced-motion branch uses animate={} while initial={opacity:0,scale:0.8} (lines 267-275), so with reduced motion the user labels stay invisible. Cursor icons are defined inline inside render (lines 222-360), so they remount on every 100ms tick and AnimatePresence cannot track them.
a11y: Purely decorative with no live region for presence changes. Status dots only have a title.
api: forwardRef, but props are not passed to the DOM correctly (no HTML attribute type). The users prop is copied into state once and never re-synced (line 101). Avatars have no fallback.
ssr: Has 'use client'. Uses @/ path aliases (works only if the bundler resolves the tsconfig paths).
fake_complexity: 'realTimeMode' is a Math.random walk every 100ms with random isActive and action (lines 106-143). It ships with hard-coded 'Collaborative Workspace / Section A / Section B' demo copy in the component body (lines 429-463). soundEnabled defaults to true and plays type/select sounds on every simulated tick.
target: collaboration/GlassCollaborativeCursor
justification: This is the shadowed duplicate. src/index.ts:699 exports the collaboration/ version under the same name, so this file is unreachable for consumers but still certified and storied (18 stories). It is a random-walk demo with baked-in placeholder copy, sounds that play on by default, inline component definitions that remount every tick, and a reduced-motion bug that hides labels. Delete it.
screenshot_review: Image rendering through the Read tool returned empty in this session, so the review used grayscale pixel statistics. Desktop luminance mean is 243 with std 19; mobile mean is 240 with std 31 (0-255). A std under about 20 on a mean around 245 means a near-white glass surface on a near-white canvas with very little tonal separation. That is the washed-out white-on-white look, not a premium layered material. The visual score is capped accordingly.

name: GlassPresenceIndicator
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell with createGlassStyle() inline on every user chip and avatar, which nests blurred glass inside blurred glass (each with its own backdrop-filter). Status colours use semantic tokens (hsl(var(--glass-color-success))), which is good. Several class names do not exist ('glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-60', 'glass-surface-subtle/20').
motion: framer-motion. The reduced-motion branch sets animate={} with initial={opacity:0,scale:0.8} (lines 207-208, 368-373, 413-417), so reduced-motion users see an invisible list and footer. The status dot pulses forever.
a11y: User chips are clickable motion.divs with no role, tabIndex or keyboard handler (lines 204-220). Status is conveyed by colour only, with no text or sr label. The typing notice is not a live region.
api: forwardRef. The users prop is copied once into state and never re-synced (line 90). theme, onStatusChange and id are unused. The prop list is large (16) but half of it is demo knobs.
fake_complexity: realTimeSync randomly flips isTyping. soundEnabled=true by default plays a 'notification' for every online user whenever presenceData or play changes, and play is a new function every render (src/utils/soundDesign.ts:549-565), so it chimes on every render after a user gesture unlocks audio.
target: GlassAvatarGroup + GlassPresenceBadge (single presence primitive)
justification: Presence (avatar plus status dot plus overflow count) is a legitimate pattern, but this version has a reduced-motion invisibility bug, mouse-only interactive chips, colour-only status, sound that fires on every render by default, and a frozen users prop. Fold it into one avatar-group/presence-badge primitive shared with GlassUserPresence and GlassLiveCursorPresence.
screenshot_review: Image rendering through the Read tool returned empty in this session, so the review used grayscale pixel statistics. Desktop luminance mean is 245 with std 8; mobile mean is 247 with std 9 (0-255). A std under about 20 on a mean around 245 means a near-white glass surface on a near-white canvas with very little tonal separation. That is the washed-out white-on-white look, not a premium layered material. The visual score is capped accordingly.

name: GlassReactionBubbles
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell. It passes createGlassStyle({...}).background, a CSS gradient string, into className (lines 441, 459, 499, 655, 701), which produces garbage class names. The bubbles, emoji selector, stats and instructions therefore have no glass material at all. There is a hard-coded neon palette.
motion: A custom 'physics' loop: one requestAnimationFrame per render, with the effect depending on bubbles (line 289), so the loop runs as setState-per-frame while any bubble exists. The demo state seeds bubbles, so it re-renders at 60fps by default. With reduced motion, the stats panel stays at opacity 0 (lines 657-658). The ambient particles loop forever.
a11y: Reaction bubbles are clickable divs with no role or keyboard support. The canvas click is mouse-only. Emoji selector buttons have no aria-label or aria-pressed. 'Click bubbles to multiply them' adds three bubbles per click, which is uncontrolled growth limited only by maxBubbles.
api: forwardRef, but HTML props are not typed. Both demoState='active' (default) and autoplay exist. The reactions prop is used only as the initial state. Both compact and contained exist.
ssr: Has 'use client'. Process env checks (JEST_WORKER_ID) are in component code.
fake_complexity: realTimeMode spawns 'Anonymous' random reactions. It ships demo users 'Aurora/Lumen/Orbit' by default. Test-environment branching lives inside the production component (lines 201-210, 216, 235, 545).
target: interactive/GlassReactionBar (keep one reaction primitive); optional effect as a recipe
justification: This is a novelty effect with a demo-on-by-default state, a setState-per-frame physics loop, invalid className usage that silently drops the glass material, test-env branches inside product code, and a reduced-motion invisibility bug. It is the third reaction component. Keep GlassReactionBar as the product primitive and drop this one, or rewrite it later as an opt-in canvas/WAAPI effect.
screenshot_review: Image rendering through the Read tool returned empty in this session, so the review used grayscale pixel statistics. Desktop luminance mean is 246 with std 8; mobile mean is 248 with std 9 (0-255). A std under about 20 on a mean around 245 means a near-white glass surface on a near-white canvas with very little tonal separation. That is the washed-out white-on-white look, not a premium layered material. The visual score is capped accordingly.

name: GlassSharedWhiteboard
material_impl: OptimizedGlass with createGlassStyle inline on the toolbar and user list. The colour palette is six near-white translucent rgba values (lines 91-98), which are invisible on the default white canvas. The default pen colour is 'var(--glass-black)' (line 141), which canvas strokeStyle cannot resolve: assignment is ignored and the previous stroke style is reused. The grid is #E5E5E5.
motion: framer-motion spring cursors. With reduced motion, animate={} still renders. There is no reduced-motion concern for drawing.
a11y: Tool buttons are labelled by emoji and title only. Size buttons render a transparent dot (glass-bg-transparent, line 555), so the size is visually invisible. The canvas has no accessible name or alternative. It is mouse events only, with no pointer/touch handlers (lines 613-616), so drawing does not work on phones or tablets.
api: forwardRef, but HTML props are not typed. strokes and users are copied into state once. Both readOnly and canDraw exist. The 'shape' tool draws a freehand line like the pen.
ssr: Has 'use client'. getComputedStyle runs in an effect only.
fake_complexity: realTimeSync generates random cursor movement and random two-point 'strokes' from other users. There is no transport or CRDT, and no DPR scaling, so lines blur on retina displays.
target: interactive/GlassWhiteboard (single whiteboard, pointer events + DPR + controlled strokes)
justification: As shipped, the whiteboard cannot draw in a visible colour from its own palette, cannot be used on touch devices, ignores devicePixelRatio, and fakes collaboration with random strokes. It duplicates interactive/GlassWhiteboard. Merge into one pointer-events whiteboard with a controlled strokes API and real colour tokens, or drop the category entirely.

name: SpatialComputingEngine
material_impl: Not a glass surface. It is a motion.div wrapper with CSS-var dot overlays. The debug HUD uses white text on a light primary surface.
motion: Six framer useSprings. enablePhysics defaults to true and starts a RAF loop that calls updateSpatialPosition -> setCurrentPosition (a new object) every frame, and the effect re-subscribes each frame because applyPhysics depends on currentPosition (lines 487-559). The result is 60fps re-renders forever, by default. useReducedMotion is called but never used (line 200). The global '@keyframes pulse' name collides with other libraries.
a11y: N/A wrapper. Pointer and touch listeners give no keyboard parity.
api: React.FC with no ref, className only. VRGlassComponent, ARGlassComponent, HoloGlassComponent and useSpatialTracking are defined but not root-exported. useSpatialTracking is a stub.
ssr: Has 'use client'. However, useState(detectSpatialContext()) is non-lazy and reads window.innerWidth during render (lines 176, 203-205), so it throws ReferenceError on server render. On mount it calls navigator.xr.requestSession without a user gesture (lines 246-285). That fails silently, or on a headset tries to enter an immersive session. getViewerPose is passed a framebuffer instead of a reference space (line 269).
fake_complexity: Self-declared '@demo DEMO / EXPERIMENTAL ... NOT backed by a real WebXR runtime' (lines 8-11). Gesture 'recognition' is pointerdown=tap and touches.length==2=pinch. Anchors are setTimeout(5000). 'Physics' clamps y to 0.
justification: This is a self-admitted mock exported from the package root. It crashes SSR via window access in render, re-renders at 60fps by default through a no-op gravity loop (the only story sets enablePhysics={false}, which hides this), requests an XR session on mount without user activation, and misuses the WebXR API. It contributes nothing to a glass design system. Remove it from the public API and from the certification set.

name: SpeedDial (+ GlassSpeedDial)
material_impl: CSS module (SpeedDial.module.css) with tokens throughout: --aura-color-glass-surface, --aura-glass-neutral-level2-backdrop-blur, --glass-filter-base and semantic colour vars. motion: CSS transitions on motion tokens with @media (prefers-reduced-motion) overrides in all three CSS modules. Staggered 30ms delays. useReducedMotion is imported but unused, which is fine because CSS handles it.
a11y: The FAB is a real button with aria-expanded, but aria-haspopup='true' implies a menu and there is no role=menu/menuitem or roving focus. The actions wrapper is aria-hidden={!open} while the actions keep tabIndex=0 (SpeedDialAction.tsx:132), so hidden but focusable elements exist when closed (an axe aria-hidden-focus violation). The global Escape listener is always attached. Focus does not move into the actions on open or return on close. ariaLabel is optional, so an icon-only FAB can ship without a name.
api: forwardRef, controlled/uncontrolled open, direction, size, positionStrategy and showBackdrop, which is MUI-like and sensible. Bug: each child's own onClick is overwritten by handleActionClick (line 277), so per-action onClick props (the natural API, as used in stories via {...action}) never fire, and only onActionClick(index) works. The position type includes intent/elevation/tier (types.ts:87-93), which resolvePositionStyle would dump into inline style. color 'info' is in the class map but not the type. ContrastGuard and ANIMATION imports are dead.
ssr: Has 'use client'. window and document are only touched in effects.
fake_complexity: None.
target: Merge GlassFab as the trigger; export GlassSpeedDial
justification: This is structurally the healthiest component in the shard: token-driven CSS modules, real reduced-motion support, a controlled/uncontrolled API and a forwardRef. It needs targeted fixes, not a rewrite. Fix it by chaining child onClick, applying the menu/menuitem pattern with focus management, making closed actions inert or tabIndex -1, requiring an accessible name, removing junk position keys, and exporting the glass variant. a11y: N/A.
api: Takes children and fallback. Not exported from the ./ssr or ./client subpaths where consumers would look for it.

name: DimensionalGlass

tests.nature: templated smoke/axe/className/snapshot

screenshot_review: The PNG could not be rendered in this session (the image reader returned empty, and a JPEG conversion did too). Certification DOM metrics show 11 visible elements and 6 glass elements, with story copy 'Dimensional clarity'. Nothing beyond a single card is rendered. No tilt or depth can be seen in a static capture, and the code never implements tilt.
material_impl: Shared primitive. The default branch uses OptimizedGlass (159-170), and material='liquid' uses LiquidGlassMaterial (91-113) with quality 'ultra' by default (110). Padding, z-index and depth are built as dynamic class strings: `p-${Math.round(padding/4)}` (185), `z-${...}` (198) and `[transform:${depthTransform}]` (177). No build step generates these, so the padding/zIndex props do nothing on the OptimizedGlass branch. borderRadius is bucketed into md/lg/xl and ignores the actual value (189-195).
motion: Motion primitive fadeIn (82-83) with useReducedMotion gating (54-55). The animation classes 'animate-pulse-subtle' (86), 'animate-dimensional-float' (130) and 'transform-style-preserve-3d' (176) have no CSS rule anywhere in src. maxTilt is only written to a CSS var (139) that nothing reads, so the 'dimensional tilt' does not exist.
a11y: interactive defaults to true (36), which adds cursor-pointer, liftOnHover and press to a plain div with no role, tabIndex or keyboard handling. Every instance looks clickable but is not operable.
api: forwardRef: yes. className is applied twice, to both the Motion wrapper (87) and the surface (132/200), so user layout classes are duplicated. style passes through. opacity, animationConfig and motionSensitivity are destructured and ignored (30, 45-47). elevation accepts a string or number and is coerced with an `any` mapper that is copy-pasted into five sibling files.
ssr: 'use client'. No module-scope window access. The liquid branch pulls in LiquidGlassMaterial.
fake_complexity: Advertised as 'enhanced depth and dimensional effects'. In practice it is OptimizedGlass plus a translateZ with no perspective parent, so the translateZ has no visible effect, and the tilt is unimplemented.
target: GlassCard / OptimizedGlass elevation+depth props
justification: This is a thin wrapper over OptimizedGlass. Its distinguishing props (tilt, depth, padding, zIndex) are either unimplemented or emitted as dynamic utility classes that never resolve. Real depth should come from the material's elevation/depth tokens on one canonical surface. Keep a deprecated alias that maps elevation and depth to GlassCard.

Dynamic `duration-[${ms}ms]` (158), `rounded-[${n}px]` (168) and `p-${n}` (172) classes do not resolve.

a11y: interactive defaults to true (35): cursor-pointer and a hover lift on a non-focusable div. Overlay opacities were deliberately lowered for label contrast (216, 232, 253). ContrastGuard is imported but unused (15).

Fold the noise and specular layers into the material engine as an opt-in texture, then delete the wrapper and its five-way copy-pasted mapping code.

name: GlassDepthLayer (+ GlassDepthScene, LayeredGlassStack, useDepthAnimation, DEFAULT_DEPTH_CONFIGS: non-root internals)

tests.nature: templated smoke/axe/snapshot

screenshot_review: The image could not be rendered. The story mounts layer='mid' with initial={false}, parallax off and hover off (stories:44-48), so the certified frame avoids every motion and parallax path. That makes the frame unrepresentative of default usage.
material_impl: Calls createGlassStyle({intent:'neutral', elevation:'level2'}) (151-153). Every layer gets the identical style: the per-layer config opacity, blur, brightness and shadow (44-124) are never applied, and the useMemo depends on [config] without using it. Only config.transform is used, and only on hover or parallax. The 'overlay' shadow uses a malformed rgba(var(--glass-color-black) / var(--glass-opacity-50)) (122).
motion: framer-motion initial/animate y:20 fade on every mount (158-159). useReducedMotion is called (141) and its result never used, so reduced motion is not honored. whileHover sets transform to translateZ(-50px) scale(1.1) plus a lift (162). Without a perspective parent, translateZ is a no-op and the scale jumps. Parallax writes element.style.transform directly in onMouseMove (180), fighting framer's own transform. useDepthAnimation delays by zIndex*0.1, which is 7 seconds for the overlay layer (286).
a11y: No role, focus or keyboard handling. The mouse-only parallax is fine as decoration. The reduced-motion violation is real.
api: forwardRef: yes. style is explicitly Omitted from props (33), so consumers cannot style it and the glass style always wins. children is required. customConfig fields other than transform are ignored. GlassDepthScene, LayeredGlassStack and useDepthAnimation are exported from the module but not from root.
ssr: 'use client'. framer-motion import. No window access at module scope.
fake_complexity: An 8-level 'depth system' whose opacity, blur, brightness and shadow tables are dead data. Every layer renders the same level2 glass.
target: OptimizedGlass elevation/depth tokens
justification: The depth table is not wired to the material: every layer renders identical level2 glass. Reduced motion is computed and ignored, the 3D transforms have no perspective context, and imperative style writes conflict with framer-motion. Depth belongs in the elevation token scale of the canonical material, not in a parallel layer enum.

name: TreeItem (+ GlassTreeItem)

Label color is hard-coded to rgba(var(--glass-color-black)/.95) !important, and the selected state is also forced black, so it is unreadable on dark themes.
motion: Height animates via CSS transition on a measured scrollHeight plus a perspective rotateX(-5deg) on collapse. useReducedMotion only removes the transition; the rotateX transform still applies. A SpringConfig is computed (finalSpringConfig) and never used. Measured height is captured once per expand, so expanding a nested child does not grow the parent's fixed height and the content is clipped.
a11y: role=treeitem sits on the <li>, but focus goes to the inner div, so the focused element has no role and the treeitem itself is never focused. Collapsed children stay in the DOM at height 0 with tabIndex=0, so keyboard users tab into invisible items. The expand toggle is a div with onClick and aria-hidden: double-click and ArrowRight are the only alternatives. Focus-visible box-shadow ring exists in CSS.
api: forwardRef, className/style. color is applied to a CSS var. animationConfig/motionSensitivity are ignored. Throws outside TreeView.
ssr: 'use client'; useLayoutEffect + requestAnimationFrame produce an SSR warning on the server.
fake_complexity: Partial: it imports a spring-physics config path that does nothing.
target: data-display/GlassTreeView
justification: This item has several defects: focus lands on a role-less div, hidden children remain tabbable, nested expansion clips because of the fixed measured height, the label is forced to black with !important, and a dead spring config is computed. It is not worth polishing in isolation. Fold the compound child API into the canonical tree.

material_impl: Wraps GlassButton inside a div that also gets createGlassStyle({neutral, level2, high}), which stacks two glass surfaces (double blur and border). Ripple color comes from a hard-coded RGB map (default white at 0.3 alpha).

Odd aria-pressed string coercion.

justification: Ripple is a press-feedback option, not a component. GlassButton already contains ripple code, and wrapping it here double-stacks glass and splits prop passthrough. Move a pointer-event-based ripple into GlassButton behind a prop and delete this wrapper.

material_impl: Overlay div with color-mix tints from a hard-coded RGB map plus mix-blend-mode: overlay. With glass=true it spreads createGlassStyle({elev:2}) onto the overlay. The overlay sits at z-index 1 above children.
motion: CSS pulse for loading, gated by reduced motion. OK.
a11y: Purely visual: no role=status, no aria-busy for loading, no aria-disabled for disabled. Communicates state by color only (WCAG 1.4.1). The 'warning' and 'info' states declared in types fall to transparent.
api: forwardRef, className/style. size, animated, glassVariant and blurStrength are declared and leak to the DOM. State naming mixes interaction states (hover/active/focus) with status (success/error).
fake_complexity: Mild: states are advertised but not rendered.
target: data-state attributes + tokenized state layers on the base surface primitive
justification: Painting an overlay with blend modes over arbitrary children is not how a premium system expresses state. State layers belong in each component's token set, keyed by data-state. Half of the declared states render nothing, and there is no assistive-tech exposure.

name: VisualFeedback
material_impl: CSS module keyframes (pulse/glow/highlight/bounce/shake/ripple). The optional glass overlay uses createGlassStyle. Ripple color comes from a hard-coded RGB map.
motion: All effects are infinite CSS loops while active; reduced motion disables the class. Infinite shake/bounce is a usability smell. The ripple setTimeout has no cleanup.
a11y: No semantics. type and message props are declared but never rendered, so the 'feedback' is invisible to assistive tech.
api: forwardRef with manual ref merge. type, message and position are declared, unused, and leak to the DOM (message as an attribute).
fake_complexity: Mild: the message/type/position props suggest a toast-like feedback system that does not exist.
target: motion preset tokens (src/animations) applied via a shared Motion primitive
justification: This is a grab-bag effect wrapper that duplicates motion presets and ripple code elsewhere. Its feedback props (message/type/position) are unimplemented. A premium system exposes named motion tokens, not an infinite-shake div.

name: GlassAdvancedDataViz

tests.note: templated smoke/axe/snapshot test, identical to other generated tests

material_impl: Wraps the Glass primitive, but the chart internals are hand-rolled SVG with a palette that mixes tokens with hard-coded hex (#8B5CF6, #EC4899, #06B6D4, ...), stroke='white' point outlines, and a gray grid. Raw Tailwind classes (flex, px-3, rounded) are mixed with glass-* utilities.
motion: The enableAnimation flag only adds a 'transition-all duration-300' class to the path. No reduced-motion handling.
a11y: The SVG has no role, title, desc or data table alternative. The tooltip is mouse-only, and points and bars are click-only (no keyboard). Export and legend buttons are real buttons (good). The drill-down remove button is a bare '✕' without a label.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, className only. type supports 'pie' | 'scatter' | 'heatmap' but only line/bar/combo render, so the other types silently render empty axes. enablePan, enableCrosshair and showDataLabels are unused. PNG/SVG export does nothing. Legend toggling is broken: processedData filters out hidden series and the legend maps processedData, so a hidden series disappears from the legend and cannot be re-enabled.
ssr: 'use client'. window.innerWidth is read during render when the tooltip is visible. Static pattern id='grid' collides across instances. onWheel calls preventDefault on React's passive wheel listener, which is ineffective and logs a warning. Hit-testing uses unscaled coordinates while the SVG is CSS-scaled (maxWidth:100%), so the tooltip misfires on narrow screens.
fake_complexity: Yes, moderately: the 'Advanced' features (pie, heatmap, scatter, pan, crosshair, PNG/SVG export) are declared and absent.
target: charts/GlassChart (single chart system)
justification: This is a fourth chart implementation with a broken legend toggle, half of its declared chart types missing, grid lines drawn on top of the data, and no accessible data alternative. Pixel analysis of the certification screenshot shows a single pale grey line inside a light frame with 0% chromatic pixels, so the hex and token palette does not even resolve to color in the certified run. Fold any useful drill-down/filter/export logic into the canonical chart and delete this file.
evidence: src/components/visualization/GlassAdvancedDataViz.tsx:324,940 legend maps filtered data -> cannot re-show series

name: VoiceGlassControl (+ VoiceGlassDemo alias, GlassVoiceCommands)
material_impl: Bespoke inline voiceSurfaceStyle with hard-coded rgba(255,255,255,.14/.28/.3) plus glass-backdrop-blur-lg classes. Raw Tailwind (bg-blue-500, bg-white/20, w-10 h-6) is used for the toggle switch, and many glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-* class names look invented.
motion: framer-motion. Enter animations are gated by reduced motion, but whileHover scale 1.05 on the main panel is not gated, and the initial opacity:0 states remain under reduced motion because animate={} never resolves them to 1. Under reduced motion, panels can stay invisible.
a11y: The primary mic toggle is an icon-only button with no aria-label. Settings and Help panels have no role=dialog, focus trap or Escape handling. The feedback toggle is a button without role=switch or aria-checked. Status text is not in a live region. Labels are not associated with inputs (no htmlFor).
api: Default-export function component, no forwardRef, no style passthrough, fixed positioning hard-coded. wakeWord defaults to 'Hey Genesis' (a product brand leak).
ssr: 'use client'; window access is inside effects (OK). It overwrites the global speechSynthesis.onvoiceschanged handler twice (hook and component) and nulls it on unmount, clobbering other consumers.
fake_complexity: Yes, completely: SpeechRecognition is never instantiated, isListening/transcript/wakeWordDetected are never set to true or non-empty, and the local setLastCommand only speaks the feedback text without updating state. The only real capability is speechSynthesis TTS. The file header admits it is a DEMO with mock data, yet it is root-exported twice (VoiceGlassControl and VoiceGlassDemo).
target: move to examples/ (non-published) or rebuild on interactive/GlassVoiceInput with a real recognition adapter
justification: This is a mock dressed as a product feature. Recognition is never wired, state setters are never called, and the brand-specific wake word ships in a public library. It is root-exported under two names. Its a11y gaps (unlabeled icon toggle, non-dialog modals) would fail review. Remove it from the published surface.

name: GlassChartsDemo (+ GlassDefs, chartGlass, axisTokens internals)
material_impl: Static inline SVGs with hard-coded hex (#70d6ff, #a78bfa, #34d399) and rgba(226,232,240,.14) gridlines tuned for dark backgrounds. chartGlass tokens assume white-on-dark (var(--glass-white) 88%) text, so they are illegible on light themes. The comments reference Recharts and an 'admin portal' from another codebase.
motion: None. useReducedMotion and ANIMATION are imported and unused.
a11y: SVGs have role=img + aria-label (good) but carry no data.
api: Function component, className/children only.
fake_complexity: Yes: the subtitle says 'Live chart primitives' over hard-coded arrays of static paths.
target: docs/storybook example for charts/GlassChart
justification: This is a static marketing illustration published as a root component. The fixed three-column grid does not collapse on mobile, and the colors are hex literals. Recharts helpers copied from another app (GlassDefs/chartGlass) belong in the chart system's theme layer, if anywhere.

name: GlassLinkButton
material_impl: Mostly raw Tailwind (bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-500/80 to-purple-500/80, border-white/20, focus-visible:ring-blue-500/60, h-10 px-4), which consumers without Tailwind JIT scanning node_modules will not get. Two stacked createGlassStyle overlays plus a mask-composite border trick. Hard-coded blue-to-purple gradient: a 2021 'glassmorphism' look, not a token-driven system.
motion: Tailwind transitions and an active translate; no reduced-motion handling.
a11y: Native <a> with a focus-visible ring (Tailwind-dependent). disabled:* classes do nothing on an anchor, so there is no aria-disabled handling. The h-8 small size is under 44px despite the touch-target class.
api: forwardRef, className passthrough. intent is ignored for variant=primary, and the noise prop is unused. Prop naming (variant/intent/size) differs from GlassButton.
fake_complexity: No.
target: GlassButton asChild (or GlassButton href)
justification: GlassButton already supports asChild, so a separate link button with its own Tailwind-only styling fragments the button family and breaks for non-Tailwind consumers. Replace it with <GlassButton asChild><a/></GlassButton> and remove this file.

name: GlassPrismComparison
material_impl: Bespoke: createGlassStyle in compact mode; elsewhere inline rgba(255,255,255,.24), boxShadow rgba(125,211,252,.6), and gradient text set imperatively via ref callbacks. Many class names look invented or duplicated (glass-gradient-primary repeated 3x in one string, glass-inline-glass-block, glass-via-yellow-400). Text is forced to black via local token overrides and rgb(15,23,42) literals.
motion: Heavy framer-motion: around 20 infinite floating particles, an infinite gradient shift, pulsing text-shadow, a rotating custom cursor, and refraction streaks. Most animations are gated by reduced motion, but the 4.2s auto-rotate setInterval is not. A leftover dead prismStyle object is computed inside the useEffect.
a11y: glass-cursor-none hides the system cursor. Interaction is mouse-only (no keyboard or touch control of the prism). Auto-rotating content has no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2). Category buttons are fine.
api: Takes only HTMLAttributes; content is hard-coded.
ssr: 'use client'; seededRandom for deterministic particles (good); ResizeObserver guarded.
fake_complexity: Yes: it hard-codes AuraOne marketing claims ('10,000x Quantum-accelerated training', '100% Formal verification', 'ISO 26262, DO-178C, FDA Automatic certification') and calls a CSS clip-path divider a 'prism'.
target: AuraOne marketing site repo
justification: This is a product landing-page section with unverifiable regulatory and performance claims embedded as constants. It does not belong in a design-system package. It is mouse-only, auto-rotating, and hides the cursor. If a 'prism reveal' material effect is wanted, build it as a WipeSlider variant over the real Liquid Glass primitive.

name: GlassWipeSlider (+ ComparisonImage, ComparisonContent, FeatureComparison, MetricsComparison, SLIDER_PRESETS, AURAONE_COMPARISON_EXAMPLES)
material_impl: Bespoke inline rgba gradients for the divider and handle (rgba(255,255,255,.28/.14), rgba(71,85,105,.x) shadows) plus glass-foundation-complete/glass-backdrop-blur-md-medium classes. Template-literal Tailwind classes such as glass-duration-[${...}ms] cannot be generated by any JIT, so they are dead. ComparisonContent's default background is raw Tailwind from-slate-900 via-blue-900.
motion: framer-motion handle with useMotionAwareAnimation (reduced-motion aware). The custom rAF momentum ignores reduced motion. handleTransform (useTransform) is computed and unused, and springX/springY are unused.
a11y: This is the best part. The container is role=slider with aria-valuemin/max/now, a rich keyboard model (arrows, shift/ctrl steps, Home/End, PageUp/Down, 0-5 presets) and SR-only instructions. Gaps: no aria-orientation for vertical, no aria-valuetext, a static id='slider-metrics' that collides across instances, and the focus ring is a pulsing border (animate-pulse) inside the handle.
api: memo only, no forwardRef. Uncontrolled only: initialPosition is read once, so PresetPositionDemo's external buttons cannot move it (a bug, visible in its own Examples). The large prop surface (compact/preview/contained/density all meaning roughly the same thing) indicates patch-on-patch. Exports vendor-specific AURAONE_COMPARISON_EXAMPLES (Scale AI, OpenAI Gym).
ssr: 'use client'; document listeners attach only while dragging (good). React onTouchStart preventDefault on a passive listener triggers a warning.
fake_complexity: Low: the slider works, but 'momentum' and 'snapping' only run when release velocity exceeds 0.1.
duplicates: no canonical compare slider elsewhere (rg found none)
target: media/GlassCompareSlider (controlled value/onValueChange, forwardRef, pointer events, shared LiquidGlass handle)
justification: This is the only real, working before/after slider in the library, with a solid keyboard model, so it is worth keeping as a concept. The implementation needs a rebuild: controlled API, Pointer Events instead of mouse+touch pairs, forwardRef, collapse compact/preview/contained/density into one size prop, remove dead springs and impossible JIT classes, and render the handle and divider with the shared glass primitive. Strip the AuraOne/competitor marketing constants. Pixel analysis of the screenshot shows a near-white field with the faint divider barely distinguishable (min luminance about 233 in the downsample), so it does not currently read as a premium material.

name: GlassWipeSliderExamples (+ AuraOneVsScaleAIComparison, VerticalFeatureComparison, PerformanceMetricsComparison, ImageBeforeAfterComparison, PresetPositionDemo, GlassWipeSliderShowcase)
material_impl: Composition of GlassWipeSlider plus many invented or duplicated class names (glass-gradient-primary x3, glass-h-500px, glass-via-red-glass-opacity-50) and raw Tailwind (bg-blue-500/20, text-blue-300).
motion: Inherits; a framer chip uses an exit animation without AnimatePresence, so the exit never runs.
a11y: Wrapping divs are role=region with labels (fine). Preset buttons do not move the slider because it is uncontrolled.
api: Demo functions; not a component API.
fake_complexity: Yes: 'Real metrics from enterprise customers' over invented numbers; AuraOne vs Scale AI / OpenAI Gym marketing copy; placeholder 'Image Content' SVGs.
target: GlassWipeSlider stories (neutral content)
justification: This is showcase/marketing content with fabricated customer metrics and competitor naming, living in src/. It is not root-exported but is still compiled and storied. Move any neutral examples into stories and delete it.

name: MotionAwareGlass (+ MotionAwareGlassCard/Button/Input, useMotionAwareGlassStyles)
material_impl: Raw Tailwind and pseudo-classes: 'backdrop-filter' with no blur value, bg-white/5, bg-white/8 (not a default Tailwind step), border-white/15, plus legacy glass-subtle/glass-strong classes. The useMotionAwareGlassStyles variants all return the same background token. No shared primitive.
motion: framer-motion variants from lib/motionPrimitives, keyed on MotionPreferenceContext. Reduced motion is actually wired (good), but every instance renders an sr-only 'Motion reduced for accessibility' string, which screen readers announce repeatedly as noise.
a11y: With asButton it renders a div with role=button and tabIndex. Its onKeyDown overrides any consumer onKeyDown and calls onClick with a KeyboardEvent cast as any. MotionAwareGlassInput is a div, not an input. interactive=true makes non-button cards tabbable with no role.
api: forwardRef. Variant names (base/subtle/strong/card/button/input) conflate component types with surface levels.
fake_complexity: Mild: 'Input' and 'Button' variants are styled divs.
target: Glass primitive + motion preset prop (reduced motion handled centrally)
justification: Motion preference should be a property of the primitive and the motion tokens, not a parallel family of surfaces, buttons and inputs. This file builds fake buttons and inputs from divs, relies on Tailwind classes that are not part of the token system, and emits SR noise in every instance.

name: Icon set (components.tsx: ~160 glyphs, ~220 exports, GlassIcon named registry, *Icon aliases)

tests.note: getByLabelText passes even though the svg is aria-hidden

material_impl: Not glass. 24x24 stroke icons via createGlassIcon, with names and API mirroring lucide-react. Glyphs are hand-approximated: Settings is a sunburst rather than a gear, CommandIcon maps to Search, FolderKanban = Folder, MessageSquare = MessageCircle path, and Snowflake is a 3-line asterisk. Many aliases point to the same glyph.
motion: None (Loader2 has no spin).
a11y: aria-hidden is forced to true unless explicitly overridden, even when the consumer passes aria-label or title, so labeled icons vanish from the accessibility tree. The test checks getByLabelText, which does not account for aria-hidden, so it gives false assurance.
api: forwardRef via factory, size/color/strokeWidth/absoluteStrokeWidth (lucide parity). It is published at subpaths ./icons/* plus root. The named GlassIcon registry falls back silently to Circle for unknown names.
ssr: Pure SVG; no 'use client' needed; tree-shakable per export.
fake_complexity: No, but the glyph quality is not first-party: it is a lucide look-alike drawn by approximation.
duplicates: inline chevron SVGs duplicated in TreeItem.tsx and GlassWipeSlider.tsx
target: first-party icon set (designed on a grid with optical stroke rules) or adopt lucide as a dependency
justification: Removing the third-party dependency was reasonable and the factory API is fine. The glyphs, however, are rough approximations, several are semantically wrong (Settings, Command), and the aria-hidden-by-default override breaks labeled icons. A premium system needs a deliberately drawn icon family with a gallery story and visual regression. Either commission or draw a real set, or depend on lucide and theme it.

name: createGlassIcon (factory)
material_impl: N/A. Stroke SVG with currentColor.
motion: N/A
a11y: Line 59 sets aria-hidden={rest['aria-hidden'] ?? true} after spreading rest. It should default to hidden only when no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title is present, and should add role='img' when labeled.
api: forwardRef, displayName, absoluteStrokeWidth scaling (correct math). Clean.
fake_complexity: No.
justification: This is a small, correct factory and one of the cleaner files in this shard. The one fix needed is labeled-icon semantics (role=img + aria-hidden=false when labeled), plus a test that asserts accessibility-tree exposure.

name: createIcon (re-export shim)
material_impl: N/A
motion: N/A
a11y: N/A
api: Re-exports createGlassIcon. rg finds no importer anywhere in src.
fake_complexity: N/A
target: src/icons/createGlassIcon.tsx
justification: This is a dead 6-line shim with no importers.

name: DismissableLayer (alias GlassDismissableLayer)
material_impl: Headless, no styling.
motion: n/a
a11y: Escape/outside pointer/outside focus dismissal with preventDefault-able callbacks — solid Radix-like contract. No layer stack: nested layers all dismiss on a single Escape (each registers its own document keydown and none stops propagation); a click inside a nested portal-rendered child layer counts as outside for the parent. disableOutsidePointerEvents sets body pointer-events:none with no stacking, so two layers restore in wrong order.
api: forwardRef with ref merge, HTMLAttributes passthrough. Effect deps on inline callbacks re-subscribe every render (harmless but churny). `style` placed before {...props} fine.
fake_complexity: None.
duplicates: Outside-click/escape logic re-implemented in GlassModal, GlassPopover, GlassDropdownMenu, hooks (useClickOutside), FocusTrap onEscape.
justification: A correct, small headless primitive that should be the single dismissal engine for all overlays. Needs a layer stack (only top-most layer handles Escape/outside), portal-aware 'inside' detection, and adoption by Modal/Popover/Dropdown to remove duplicated logic.

name: FocusTrap (+ useFocusTrap)
stories: src/primitives/focus/FocusTrap.stories.tsx (2 empty auto-generated stories: 'A glass morphism focustrap component.')
material_impl: Headless.
motion: n/a
a11y: Serious bug: default `exclude = []` (L65) creates a new array each render, so getFocusableElements/focusFirst/handleTabKey identities change every render; the main effect (L211-253) therefore tears down and re-runs on every parent re-render — cleanup restores focus to the pre-trap element and setup re-captures it and autofocuses the first element after 0ms. Inline onEscape (used at GlassHeader.tsx:1131, GlassSearchInterface.tsx:507) has the same effect. Any state update in the parent yanks focus to the first focusable. In GlassSearchInterface the trap wraps only the results list (L507-511), so the focusin guard (L256-276) also pulls focus away from the search input outside it. When exclude is non-empty, the visibility filter is skipped entirely (L83-87). 'details' in selector duplicates summary targets. Sentinels are aria-hidden yet tabbable.
api: Not forwardRef, no className/style, wrapper div unstyled; useFocusTrap hook duplicates the entire logic with slightly different semantics (no outside-focus wrap on Tab).
fake_complexity: None, but buggy.
duplicates: FocusScope (canonical), utils/a11yEnhancers.tsx:179 FocusTrap, hooks/extended/useGlassFocus setupFocusTrap, utils/focus.ts.
target: FocusScope (src/primitives/FocusScope.tsx)
justification: Internal but load-bearing: GlassSelect, GlassPopover, GlassHeader, GlassMobileNav and GlassSearchInterface all depend on it, and its unstable-dependency effect causes focus to jump on every parent re-render. Replace all call sites with FocusScope (trapped, loop, restoreFocus) and delete this file and its placeholder stories.

Modulo-by-zero yields NaN index when no focusables.
api: Imports React unused; RovingTabindex class duplicates primitives/RovingFocusGroup.

name: ScreenReader family (ScreenReader, ScreenReaderOnly, LiveRegion, announce, useAnnounce, DescribedBy, LabelledBy, LoadingAnnouncement, ValidationAnnouncement)
material_impl: None; mixes `sr-only` (Tailwind) and `glass-sr-only` classes inconsistently (L69, L204, L267).
motion: n/a
a11y: Multiple defects: DescribedBy/LabelledBy generate Math.random ids during render (L259-260, L287) -> new id every render and SSR hydration mismatch (should be useId). LiveRegion uses role='region' with no accessible name (L121) — wrong role for a live region. useAnnounce returns a new `announce` function each render, so LoadingAnnouncement/ValidationAnnouncement effects (deps include announce, L327-334, L358) re-announce on every parent re-render; ValidationAnnouncement also re-fires whenever a new errors array instance is passed. Live region nodes are created on mount and immediately written to, which many screen readers skip.
api: Plain functions, no forwardRef; ScreenReaderOnly supports `as`.
ssr: Math.random ids break hydration; announce() guards document.
fake_complexity: None.
duplicates: components/accessibility/GlassA11y GlassScreenReader (root-exported), utils/a11yEnhancers.tsx:573 LiveRegion, utils/a11y.ts announce helpers.
target: One public a11y module (VisuallyHidden + LiveAnnouncer provider) in components/accessibility; merge GlassScreenReader and a11yEnhancers LiveRegion
justification: Unexported duplicate of announcement utilities that exist in at least two other places, with hydration-unsafe ids, a mis-roled live region and re-announcement loops. Consolidate into one VisuallyHidden + single persistent LiveAnnouncer provider using useId.

name: FocusScope (alias GlassFocusScope)
material_impl: Headless.
motion: n/a
a11y: Trap + loop + autofocus + restore focus. Bug: with loop=true and trapped=false, the document-level Tab handler pulls focus into the scope from anywhere on the page when activeElement is outside (L113-125), hijacking global tab order. focusin preventDefault is a no-op (focusin is not cancelable, L133). No scope stack for nested scopes.
api: forwardRef, HTMLAttributes passthrough, Radix-like onMountAutoFocus/onUnmountAutoFocus.
fake_complexity: None.
duplicates: FocusTrap (same shard) + useFocusTrap, utils/a11yEnhancers FocusTrap, utils/focus.ts, hooks/extended/useGlassFocus setupFocusTrap — at least 4 focus-trap implementations.

justification: This is the better-designed of the focus primitives (forwardRef, cancelable mount/unmount events, used by GlassMenuPrimitive/DropdownMenu/SelectCompound) and should be the single canonical trap. Fix loop-without-trap hijacking, add a scope stack, then migrate the other trap implementations onto it.

name: GlassAdvanced
material_impl: Hybrid: class stack (glass-foundation-complete, glass-elev-N, glass-blur-*, glass-overlay-noise/specular, glass-edge, glass-glow-*) PLUS inline createGlassStyle; renders glass-layer-frost + glass-layer-ink children (L248-249). Two styling systems applied simultaneously so class-level blur/variant may be overridden by inline createGlassStyle.
motion: motion presets as CSS classes, gated by useReducedMotion (L136, L178). Wired.
a11y: Best in shard among surfaces: auto role=button + tabIndex + Enter/Space for clickable divs (L139-158), glass-focus and glass-touch-target on interactive. Gaps: contrast='on' behaves same as 'off' (only 'auto' adds a class, L184); disabled+interactive stays tabbable.
api: forwardRef + `as` polymorphism (untyped React.ElementType, props cast to any L246-247). Vocabulary elev 0-6 / variant default|primary|... / blur sm..xl differs from GlassCore (intent/elevation levelN) and OptimizedGlassAdvanced (elevation levelN/blur subtle..intense). Prop interface is named GlassProps, colliding with GlassCore's GlassProps type. composeGlassClasses helper unused outside.
fake_complexity: Low; features map to real CSS classes, though 'contrast' prop is mostly cosmetic.
target: Canonical LiquidGlass surface primitive
justification: Has the most complete interactive a11y handling of the surface primitives and real layer structure (frost/ink), which is worth harvesting, but it duplicates GlassCore/OptimizedGlass with a third prop vocabulary, double-applies class and inline material, and has auto-generated 2-story docs. Merge its a11y and overlay-layer logic into the canonical surface and retire the name.

name: OptimizedGlassAdvanced

name: MotionFramer (also Motion / GlassMotion via primitives index)

stories.quality: Template stub identical to MotionNative's; default preset is 'none' so the story animates nothing.

material_impl: None. Class hook 'motion-primitive' (:275) has no CSS.
motion: framer-motion variants with 10 presets (:172-213); presets are restrained and tasteful (12-16px slides, 0.96 scale). Reduced motion: state defaults to true and is resolved in an effect (:235-250). Critical defect: because `reduced` is true on the first render, `initial` is undefined at mount (:277-281); framer-motion only honours `initial` on mount, so when `reduced` flips to false the element is already at its resting values and animateOnMount produces NO visible animation for anyone. Only animateOnScroll (whileInView) and animateOnHover actually work. Also ~150 lines of runtime sanitizers (coerceBackgroundKey/normalizeTransitions, :73-170, :297-348) recursively copy every motion prop on every render to paper over callers passing CSS-ish easing strings and `background` shorthands.

Declares `as`, `type`, `direction` in MotionProps (:39-42) but never destructures or implements them — they leak into motion.div as invalid DOM attributes (`as="section"`, `type="slide"`). Strips a stray `consciousness` prop (:301) — evidence of upstream prop leakage being patched downstream. Easing enum uses CSS names, durations in ms; differs from MotionNative.
ssr: 'use client'; matchMedia in effect only; hard static import of framer-motion although framer-motion is an optional peer (package.json:396-398) and this module is reachable from the root barrel (src/index.ts:15).
fake_complexity: No fake claims, but 'animateOnMount' is a silent no-op as described.

justification: This is the right foundation (framer-motion, small calm presets, reduced-motion-first), and internal components already depend on it, so it should become the one Motion primitive. Implement or delete `as`/`type`/`direction`, delete the recursive prop sanitizers (fix callers instead), move presets to the shared motion tokens in presets.ts, and give it real stories that show each preset.

name: MotionNative (exported from root as `Motion`)

stories.quality: Template stub: description 'A glass morphism motionnative component.', empty argTypes/args, 'Variants' story renders a single default instance. Shows none of the 7 types, hover/click triggers, or physics.

material_impl: None (pure motion wrapper). Emits class hooks motion-element/motion-fade/... (MotionNative.tsx:355-370) that have no CSS definitions anywhere in src (rg '.motion-element' in *.css -> 0 hits).
motion: Web Animations API via element.animate (MotionNative.tsx:285-287) plus an optional rAF spring (useMultiSpring, :95-98). Reduced motion read via matchMedia in useEffect (:101-118) and respected (shouldAnimate :120). Defects: (1) delay applied twice — setTimeout(delay) at :325 and timing.delay at :279, so delay=300 waits 600ms; (2) physics mode is effectively a no-op: spring starts at {opacity:1,x:0,y:0} (:96) and targets parsed from the 'to' keyframe are also opacity 1 / translate(0,0) (:257-271), so nothing moves; (3) mount animation runs after first paint, so content flashes visible then jumps to opacity 0 and fades in (FOUC); (4) animateOnHover stopAnimation cancels on mouseleave (:308-310) so content snaps back to non-animated state; (5) useEffect deps omit type/direction/keyframes (:331).
a11y: Neutral wrapper div; onClick on a div with no role/keyboard path when animateOnClick is used. Reduced-motion honored by default (respectReducedMotion=true).

ssr: 'use client'; window access only in effect. SSR-safe, but initial server HTML is the final visual state, then client jumps to frame 0 (hydration flash).
fake_complexity: 'physics' is a fake: spring never has a non-trivial target. 'elastic'/'bounce' are plain keyframes, fine.
target: single Motion primitive built on MotionFramer + shared useReducedMotion (src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts)

Internal components (GlassMagneticButton, GlassSelectCompound) import the MotionFramer `Motion`. Delete it and point the root `Motion` at the single framer-based primitive with a deprecation alias.

name: OptimizedGlassCore (root alias OptimizedGlass; also GlassOptimized)

stories.quality: Default, ElevationLevels, IntentVariants, PerformanceTiers, HighPerformance, Showcase — the only real story set in this shard.

tests: none dedicated in src/primitives (consumed by ~180 files, so indirectly exercised)
material_impl: Shared primitive: createGlassStyle (src/core/mixins/glassMixins.ts:41) -> glassTokenUtils.buildSurfaceStyles(intent, elevation, tier) — token-driven background, backdrop-filter (both spellings), border and shadow. This is the canonical material path and is good. Hard-coded: radius scale in px (4/8/12/16/9999, :227-240) instead of radius tokens; glowColor default rgba(255,255,255,0.5) (:143) which is never used.
motion: Transitions come from createGlassStyle (`all ...ms ease-out` — animating `all` on a backdrop-filter surface is expensive). Hover lift / press / sheen via CSS classes (glass-lift-on-hover, glass-press, glass-hover-sheen exist in src/styles/glass.css). No JS motion.
a11y: Polymorphic `as` lets callers pick semantics. interactive=true adds cursor:pointer and user-select:none but no role/tabIndex/keyboard — interactive glass divs are mouse-only unless callers add semantics. focusRing relies on CSS :focus-visible.
api: forwardRef typed as React.ElementRef<any> (:133) — polymorphic typing is effectively lost. ~30 props of which many are accepted and silently ignored: glowColor, glowIntensity, hover, animation, optimization, hardwareAcceleration, intensity, depth, tint, border, blur, variant, lighting (destructured at :142-160 and never used); caustics/chromatic/parallax/refraction/adaptive/magnet/cursorHighlight only become data-* attributes (:299-305) with no implementation. Props are destructured twice (:136-175 and :245-269) plus a regex delete of glass* keys (:273-277) to stop upstream leakage. `tier` default 'high' is overloaded to mean 'auto-detect' (:181, :190).
ssr: 'use client'. SSR-safe by starting at tier 'medium' then switching after mount (:178-207) — causes a post-hydration restyle (blur/shadow change) on every high-tier device. Uses cached detectDevice (src/utils/deviceCapabilities.ts:117-190).
fake_complexity: High. 'caustics', 'chromatic', 'refraction', 'parallax', 'magnet', 'cursorHighlight', 'lighting=iridescent|volumetric|caustic', 'border=particle|neon' all advertise effects that do nothing.
target: single Glass surface primitive (merge OptimizedGlassCore + GlassCore + OptimizedGlassAdvanced + GlassAdvanced; align with LiquidGlassMaterial)
justification: This is the de-facto material workhorse (~180 importers) and its core path — tokens via createGlassStyle — is the right one. But the public API is mostly decoration: more than a dozen props are accepted and ignored, the 'advanced' flags are data attributes pretending to be effects, the radius scale bypasses tokens, and auto-tier detection restyles every surface after hydration. In 5.0 it should be the one Glass surface: intent/elevation/radius/interactive only, properly typed polymorphism (or asChild via Slot), CSS-driven tier via @supports/media queries instead of post-mount JS, and the fake flags removed with a codemod.

name: RovingFocusGroup (Root/Item) / GlassRovingFocusGroup
tests: src/primitives/native-primitives.test.tsx:195, :215 (arrow keys, Home/End, disabled skip, RTL) — no assertion on tabIndex / tab-stop memory
material_impl: n/a (headless)
motion: n/a
a11y: Arrow/Home/End/RTL handling is correct for the tested paths. Likely defect in tab-stop memory (reasoned from code, not executed): Item's register effect depends on `context` (:176-181), and the context value is re-memoized whenever currentTabStopId changes (:113-137). Every focus move therefore runs all Items' cleanups (unregisterItem nulls currentTabStopId if it was the focused id, :58-61) then re-registers them in order (registerItem sets current ?? id, :53-56), resetting the tab stop to the FIRST item. Effect: the focused item ends up with tabIndex=-1, and Tab-out/Shift-Tab-back always returns to item 1 — the core purpose of a roving tabindex. Also: item order is Map insertion order, not DOM order (:65), so dynamically inserted items navigate out of order; no typeahead; Item default element is a div with no role.
api: Compound object API (RovingFocusGroup.Root/.Item) plus named exports; forwardRef; asChild via Slot; orientation/loop/dir; no controlled currentTabStopId/onCurrentTabStopIdChange. Root passes role={props.role} then spreads props (redundant, :143-146).
fake_complexity: No.
duplicates: Hand-rolled arrow-key handling in GlassTabs.tsx, EnhancedGlassTabs.tsx, GlassToolbar.tsx, GlassMenuPrimitive.tsx, and GlassWorkspaceTabs (which has none)
justification: The right primitive to have, and keyboard movement works, but the register/unregister effect keyed on the whole context value likely breaks tab-stop persistence — the defining roving-tabindex behaviour — and the tests don't catch it. Fix by depending on stable callbacks only (split context into a stable dispatch context and a state context), order items by compareDocumentPosition, add controlled state and typeahead, add a tabIndex/Tab-return test, then make every tabs/toolbar/menu/radio-group in the library consume it.
